note: The stage driver's head, composited over the coach. Doc 43 part one line 97 and part two's driver-head row; Q55, as unblocked. He is NOT a mover -- he is baked into the coach's own frames, and only his head separates -- so this is an overlay at a rect over a body that never swaps, exactly the shape doc 43 gives Thad's talk.
rectNote:
[488, 6, 53, 45], MEASURED BY MATCHING THE OVERLAY AGAINST THE COACH'S OWN BAKED HEAD OVER THE WHOLE UPPER COACH -- x 300-700, y 0-200 -- rather than over a small window around a rect somebody already believed. Closed-door and open-door frames agree to a pixel: [488,6] err 24.3 and [488,6] err 24.0, and the next four candidates in each are within 1px of it.

IT WAS [409, 10] AND THAT IS 79 PIXELS TOO FAR LEFT. The overlay landed out on the coach roof, clear of the driver entirely, so the coach's own head stayed visible and the player saw TWO DRIVERS. Every previous fix adjusted a rect that was in the wrong place to begin with: this file's rectNote records a height wrong by thirty-five rows, and 0e6a24c removed a rectFor override 12px right and 9px up. Both were real and neither could have worked.

HOW ALL THREE MISSED IT, INCLUDING THE SEARCH THAT FOUND IT LAST: every measurement was taken in a window centred on the rect under suspicion. A +/-30px search around [409,10] returns [385,40] at err 43.8 -- a confident answer from inside a wrong neighbourhood, and it agreed across both door states, which made it look corroborated. The rect only fell out when the search stopped assuming the answer was near the belief. R5p: the window was inherited from the record rather than derived from the artefact.

VERIFIED BY COMPOSITING, not by the error figure. At [409,10] a second head appears on the roof; at [488,6] the overlay covers the baked head and there is one driver.

All three states are 53x45, so one rect serves them. There is no rectFor and there should not be one: the head does not move between door states -- matching the closed-door head into the open-door frame returns offset (0,0).
rectForNote:
REMOVED, AND THE MEASUREMENT SAYS WHY. rectFor carried an override [421, 1, 53, 45] for idle/door-open, 12px right and 9px up from the base rect. The driver's head does not move between the two states: matching the closed-door head against the open-door frame over a 51x51 search returns offset (0,0) at a mean absolute error of 0.40, and no other offset comes close. So the override painted a second head up and to the right of the one already there, which is the two-drivers report AGAIN -- this file's own rectNote records the first instance, where the HEIGHT was wrong by thirty-five rows.

That fix corrected the base rect and the override's height, and the base rect was then verified by cross-correlation. THE OVERRIDE'S POSITION WAS NEVER RE-MEASURED, because the bug it caused had been declared closed. One rect was checked, the other inherited the belief that it was fine.

The base rect is correct for both states. If a state ever genuinely does move the driver, measure the offset the way the base rect was measured and record the number here alongside it -- do not reintroduce an override from a drawing's appearance.
statesNote:
WHICH STATE, AND WHEN, IS DOC 43 LINE 97 AND IT IS CONTENT. `looking-down` while Thad speaks up at him, `speaking` on his own lines, `neutral` otherwise. Written as a speaker per state rather than as a rule in the engine, because it is a fact about this character in this scene: the driver looks down at the man addressing him, and nothing general follows from that.

IT ANSWERED A QUESTION THAT WAS ASKED WRONG. This looked like a facing problem -- Thad speaks to a driver 300px above him and the four-direction sprite set has no pose that looks up. It is not. `facingToward` already returns `right` for that geometry, which is the only right answer the art can give, and the man who moves is the driver. Q53.
